newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen reversing falls, to rise.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen reversing falls, to rise.

text.p: Copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are seen reversing more than 10 weeks of falls and could rise by anywhere from between 2,000-6,000 tonnes, Far East metal traders said on Friday.
Aluminium stocks, on the other hand, are expected to slide by 3,000-4,000 tonnes when the LME report is released at 0900 GMT, the traders said.
"Copper should start going up," a trader for a Singapore-based metal trading firm said.
"There's a lot of physical stock moving to warehouse areas," another dealer said.

But one dealer said that while copper is expected to rise by as much as 6,000 tonnes, he would not be surprised if stocks fell by up to 20,000 tonnes because of uncertainty regarding the amount of material moving to warehouses.
"The uncertainty is about how much material is going to the LME. That's why there's such a stock variation of 6,000 tonnes up and 20,000 tonnes down," the dealer said.
Around 10,000 tonnes of copper has arrived in Singapore-based warehouses over the past week and at least 5,000 tonnes more is expected to arrive in the coming week.
A majority of the material has come in from China," one dealer said.
But only a fraction of the material has been placed on warrant. The amount of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 7,925 tonnes on Tuesday, down 700 tonnes from last Friday's level.
Three month copper prices were quoted by Singapore metal dealers at around US$2,255/60 a tonne at 0200 GMT, little changed from the kerb close in London on Thursday of $2,255.
Aluminium was priced at around $1,552/57 a tonne at 0200 GMT against the kerb close on the LME yesterday of $1,555 a tonne, dealers said.
